next_authority.question: Does the current-face prescribed-head residual converge as the bottom-adjacent layer thickness is reduced below 10 cm while the rest of the C5A workload and closure remain fixed?

scientific_interpretation: The C5A blocking signed-flux residual is not a timestep-integration floor. The dt=1e-4 to 2.5e-5 bottom-flux shift is about 4.68e-6 of the remaining current-face Reference residual, and the signed bias converges with estimated second order to approximately -4.23448e-6 cm/d.

Adding lower-zone states upward from R5 to R16 does not affect the mechanism materially. R8 and R16 are exactly identical in the diagnostic bottom-flux series at dt=2.5e-5; R5-to-R16 differences are also about 5.86e-6 of the Reference residual.
The residual is active only during prescribed-head phases. During HOLD the current-face R16 flux error is effectively machine zero.

The pre-existing BOUNDARY_FACE counterfactual is highly sensitive but much worse, changing the flux series by more than 337 times the current-face residual and increasing pooled RMSE from about 2.97e-5 to about 1.00e-2 cm/d.

Therefore C5B does not justify replacing CURRENT_LAYER_FACE. It localizes the remaining discrepancy to the prescribed-head boundary response while leaving one unresolved spatial question: every tested lower-zone ladder retained a 10-cm bottom-adjacent layer.
A bottom-cell-thickness refinement test is required before attributing the residual to the closure algebra itself.
